issues.t: Turbo oil feed line can leak and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning oil smell, smoke from under the hood, or a low oil warning. Some owners had no warning before oil sprayed onto hot parts.
issues.why: The oil supply pipe and hose that feeds the left turbocharger can deteriorate and leak. Oil dripping onto the hot turbo and exhaust can catch fire.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for recall SC300. The dealer replaces the left turbo oil feed pipe and hose for free.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump can stick and cut power (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, sputtering, stalling, or the engine going into limp mode with a check engine light and fuel pressure codes.
issues.why: A valve plunger inside the high-pressure fuel pump can stick, letting fuel pressure climb too high. The engine computer then cuts power. This is the most-reported problem in NHTSA complaints for the 2018 Stinger.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall SC281. The dealer updates the engine software and inspects and replaces the pump if needed, for free. If power drops, move to a safe spot and have it checked.

issues.t: Engine bay fire risk near the ABS unit (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. You might see an ABS warning light, smell burning, or see smoke from under the hood, even while driving.
issues.why: The anti-lock brake hydraulic control unit can short internally and overheat. Kia first recalled 2019 3.3L models, then expanded the recall to 2018-2021 Stingers.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for recall SC196. Until it's done, park outside and away from buildings. The dealer installs a new fuse kit for free.

issues.t: Front wiring harness can rub through and short (recall)
issues.sym: Electrical problems, warning lights, a burning smell or smoke from the front of the engine bay.
issues.why: A sharp burr on the left front fender can cut into the front wiring harness, causing a short circuit and fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall SC170. The dealer inspects the harness, replaces it if damaged and adds a protective cover, for free.

issues.t: Oil pressure switch leaks oil into the wiring harness
issues.sym: An oil pressure warning light, oil seeping around the engine, and electrical faults when oil travels into the wiring connectors.
issues.why: The oil pressure switch can leak, and oil wicks through the attached wiring harness toward other connectors. Owners report several oil pressure warning complaints to NHTSA, and one reported a major repair to replace the switch and harness.
issues.next: If the oil pressure light comes on, stop and check the oil level. Have the switch checked early; a leaking switch is a small fix, but replacing oil-soaked wiring is a much bigger job.

issues.t: Engine misfire from spark plugs or ignition coils
issues.sym: A shaking or stumbling engine, especially under hard acceleration, a flashing check engine light, and misfire codes for one cylinder. It can return weeks after a fix.
issues.why: The turbo V6 is hard on spark plugs and coils. A worn plug or a failing coil causes a misfire. Engine tunes and higher boost make it more likely.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Moving the coil to another cylinder shows if the coil is the cause. Replace plugs as a set, and use the plug type and gap Kia specifies.

issues.t: Brake pedal vibration from warped front rotors
issues.sym: A shudder in the brake pedal or steering wheel when slowing down, especially from highway speed.
issues.why: The large front rotors can develop uneven thickness from heat. Brake vibration is a common theme in NHTSA complaints for this car.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured. Resurfacing or replacing rotors with new pads usually fixes it. Avoid holding the brakes hard right after a hard stop.

issues.t: Brake vacuum pump can be damaged on cold starts
issues.sym: A harder brake pedal than normal or a brake booster warning, often after cold starts.
issues.why: Pumping the brakes repeatedly and quickly before the engine warms up can damage the rotor inside the extra brake vacuum pump on early 2018 Stingers built before late April 2018.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Ask a Kia dealer about campaign SC204. They inspect the pump and replace its rotor and vane for free.

issues.t: Hesitation and check engine light on the 2.0 turbo
issues.sym: The engine hesitates as it warms up and the check engine light comes on with codes P053F or P0087 (fuel pressure).
issues.why: Some early 2.0L turbo Stingers built between September 2017 and March 2018 had an engine computer that caused this. Kia replaced the computer.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A Kia dealer can replace the engine computer under service action SA352.

issues.t: Coolant leak at the transmission fluid warmer
issues.sym: The coolant level drops, you see pink or green drips, or smell sweet coolant after driving.
issues.why: The connector between the transmission fluid warmer and the engine's heater pipe can leak on some early 2.0L turbo cars.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and don't let the engine overheat. A Kia dealer replaces the connector under service action SA333.

issues.t: Slow or harsh shift into gear when stopped
issues.sym: A delay or bump when moving the shifter quickly from Park or Reverse into Drive.
issues.why: The transmission software on early 2.0L turbo cars handled quick shifts while stopped poorly. Kia updated it.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer for the transmission software update in bulletin TRA077.

issues.t: Rattle from the rear hatch
issues.sym: A rattle or knock from the back of the car over bumps.
issues.why: The liftgate striker on early cars can be slightly out of position, letting the hatch move.
issues.next: A dealer can adjust the striker under bulletins BOD178 and BOD184. It's a quick fix.

issues.t: Touchscreen goes black
issues.sym: The infotainment screen goes black and stops responding.
issues.why: A software problem in the UVO 3.0 head unit. Kia released an update.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer for the update in bulletin ELE162.

issues.t: Halogen low-beam headlight goes out
issues.sym: One low-beam headlight works on and off or stops working. The bulb connector may look melted or brown.
issues.why: The connector for the halogen low-beam bulb can make poor contact and overheat. Kia has a bulletin to repair it, and owners have filed several headlight complaints.
issues.next: Check the bulb and connector. Replace a heat-damaged connector, not just the bulb, or the problem will return.

issues.t: Adaptive headlight warning from moisture
issues.sym: A warning about the turning (bending) headlights, and the headlights stop turning with the steering.
issues.why: Moisture gets into the headlight and sets a fault code for the bending light motor. Kia's fix adds a moisture absorber and a new bracket.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer to repair it under bulletin ELE255.

issues.t: Radar cruise and collision warning turn off
issues.sym: A message that smart cruise control or forward collision assist is disabled, sometimes after a minor bump or pothole.
issues.why: If the front radar sensor or its bracket shifts, the radar is misaimed and the system shuts off. Kia tells dealers to check the mounting.
issues.next: Have the radar mounting checked and the sensor calibrated, especially after any front-end damage.

issues.t: AWD warning or binding from mismatched tires
issues.sym: An AWD warning or a binding, hopping feel in tight turns on AWD cars.
issues.why: If one tire is a different size or much more worn than the others, the AWD system sees the speed difference as wheel slip.
issues.next: Replace tires as a set of four, or at least keep them the same brand, size and close in wear.

issues.t: Sunroof won't fully open or close
issues.sym: The sunroof stops partway or won't close all the way.
issues.why: The rear slide part of the sunroof mechanism can fail. Kia's bulletin replaces it.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to repair it under bulletin BOD309. Don't force the glass.

issues.t: Overhead console light or sunglass holder latch fails
issues.sym: The overhead map light stops working or the sunglass holder won't stay closed.
issues.why: Parts in the overhead console can break. Kia issued a bulletin for the repair.
issues.next: A dealer can fix it under bulletin BOD314.

issues.t: Fuel gauge doesn't read correctly
issues.sym: The fuel gauge shows the wrong level or doesn't move.
issues.why: This is one of the top problems reported for the 2021 Stinger. The fuel level sender in the tank is a common cause.
issues.next: Track mileage between fill-ups so you don't run dry, and have the fuel level sender tested.

issues.t: Sunroof glass shatters without warning
issues.sym: A loud bang and the sunroof glass breaks, sometimes while driving on the highway, with no obvious impact.
issues.why: Several owners of 2022 and 2023 models have reported to NHTSA that the panoramic sunroof glass broke suddenly. No recall has been issued.
issues.next: If it happens, pull over safely, cover the opening, and file a complaint at nhtsa.gov. Ask your insurer and Kia about coverage.

issues.t: Gasoline smell in the cabin
issues.sym: A strong smell of gas inside the car that doesn't go away.
issues.why: Owners of the 2022 Stinger have reported gas fumes. Common causes are a fuel or vapor line leak or a fault in the evaporative emissions system.
issues.next: Don't ignore a fuel smell. Have the fuel and vapor lines inspected for leaks right away.

issues.t: Heater hose clamp may be the wrong size
issues.sym: Coolant seeping at a heater hose, a dropping coolant level, or a sweet smell.
issues.why: On some 2022 3.3L cars, a clamp of the wrong diameter was fitted to one heater hose at the factory.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer to check the clamp under service action SA479.

issues.t: A/C or blower fan stops working
issues.sym: No air from the vents, or warm air when the A/C is on.
issues.why: Owners have reported failed blower motors, a wiring fault and an A/C evaporator leak on 2022 models.
issues.next: Have the blower motor, its resistor and wiring and the A/C refrigerant level checked.

issues.t: Front door pull handle comes loose
issues.sym: The grip handle on the inside of a front door comes off the door panel.
issues.why: On 2022 Stingers built between February and June 2021, the handle may not be held in place well.
issues.next: A dealer can repair it under service action SA483.

issues.t: Remote start doesn't work
issues.sym: The car won't remote start from the key fob or the Kia Access app.
issues.why: A damper on the shift lever can keep the Park switch from reading correctly, so the car doesn't know it's in Park.
issues.next: A dealer can inspect the shift lever and replace the damper under bulletin ELE294.

issues.t: Touchscreen freezes or radio won't respond
issues.sym: The radio icon or button does nothing, or the screen freezes when using wired Apple CarPlay.
issues.why: Software problems in the wide-screen navigation head unit. Kia released updates.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer for the updates in bulletins ELE303 and ELE320.

issues.t: Rattle from the headliner or sunroof area
issues.sym: A buzz or rattle from the roof area over bumps.
issues.why: The headliner can touch nearby parts and buzz. Kia's fix adds anti-noise tape. Owners also report sunroof rattles.
issues.next: A dealer can apply the fix in bulletin BOD317.
